selection_rationale: Radio contribution in France runs on AETA codecs (French maker; Scoop5 S and Scoopy+ S are the TekPractice catalog references, ScoopTeam is the current commentary unit), so AETA has three entries. Tieline and Comrex cover the main international IP codec families, and the Telos Zephyr Xstream represents the ISDN (RNIS) era that EBU Tech 3326 / N-ACIP replaced. The other devices are reference examples for each remaining sub_type: an FM/DAB+ processor (Orban OPTIMOD 5950 HD, Omnia.11), party-line, digital-wireless and IP intercom (Clear-Com Encore MS-702 + RS-701, FreeSpeak II, Riedel Bolero, Green-GO MCX), an ON-AIR signalling light (Yellowtec litt), telephone hybrids (Telos Hx2, Sonifex DHY-04S) and a dedicated mix-minus generator (Sonifex RB-MM1). Each was checked on the manufacturer's site.

key_specs.band: Digital, license free 1.9GHz DECT band; 2.4 GHz variants also exist
key_specs.beltpacks_per_system: Up to 250 (Integrated, Active Antenna); 100 (Standalone Link and Standalone 2110)
key_specs.antennas: Up to 100 per system; antenna distribution over SMPTE 2110-30 (AES67) IP (Integrated, Standalone 2110); daisy-chain or redundant-ring (Standalone Link)
key_specs.beltpack_battery: Lithium-ion removable battery pack; 17 hours typical
key_specs.beltpack_bluetooth: pair two headsets and mobile phone; add phone call into intercom channel
key_specs.beltpack_dimensions: 8.6 cm x 4.8 cm x 13.0 cm (W x D x H)

devices.notes: Intercom type: digital wireless DECT 1.9 GHz, IP-networked antennas. Antenna connector types and the codec name are not stated in the pages read. No public manual was found. 'rf-dect-1g9' is a proposed signal id.

conflicts.note: Likely 6 intercom keys + REPLY; the page wording is inconsistent.

tekpractice.sim_value_reason: Wireless system with few physical connectors on the beltpack; useful mainly as a topology concept.

devices.technology: Digital IP (Ethernet) intercom station, 1U, up to 32 communication channels, PoE (IEEE 802.3af) or DC powered, decentralised network intercom
devices.why_it_is_a_classic: Green-GO is a networked digital intercom that runs over standard Ethernet with PoE, without a central matrix frame. The MCX is its multi-channel rack station, with an XLR4 headset and XLR3 mic and line connections.
typical_uses: theatre and live-event intercom over Ethernet

key_specs.channels: Access up to 32 communication channels, plus a program audio channel and a direct user channel
key_specs.network: Two EtherCON LAN ports with integrated 100 Mbit switch
key_specs.power: Power over Ethernet compliant with IEEE 802.3af or external DC power supply; 12V DC barrel connector (secondary)
key_specs.headset_connector: 1 Neutrik XLR4-Male Headset Connector; 32 Ω to 600 Ω
key_specs.line_io: 3-pin XLR line audio input and output

devices.notes: Intercom type: digital IP (Ethernet) intercom without a central matrix. greengoconnect.com redirects to a forum, so the current site is greengocom.com. The gender of the line I/O XLR connectors is not stated and is assumed. The GPIO connector type is not stated.

values.value: 3-pin XLR microphone input with 48V phantom power
XLR3 female microphone connector optionally supplies microphones with up to 10 V of power; FrontMic Max. 10 V

conflicts.note: Product page and manual disagree on mic power voltage.

tekpractice.sim_value_reason: etherCON + PoE intercom with XLR4 headset: contrasts IP intercom with analog party-line.

devices.technology: Modular LED signalling light (Base Controller + stackable Color Segments + optional Sound Segment) driven by per-colour GPI control inputs; USB configuration via Lighthouse software
devices.why_it_is_a_classic: A modular studio signalling light used as an ON-AIR / mic-live indicator. Each colour segment is switched by its own GPI (tally) input, which makes it a simple example of console-to-light tally wiring. It is already in the TekPractice catalog.
typical_uses: ON AIR / mic-live warning outside studios

key_specs.segments: Drives up to five litt Color Segments or four Color Segments combined with one litt Sound Segment
key_specs.colors: red, green, yellow, white and blue
key_specs.control_inputs: Individual control inputs for each color (2,4 - 24VDC); GPI per color: +3V…24V
key_specs.configuration: USB port (mini-USB jack) for configuration via free Lighthouse-Software
key_specs.connector: an 8-pin terminal block with a handy Phoenix Low-Insertion Force Connector
key_specs.power: Power supply (permanent): 9V…24V; It is not possible to use USB ports for power supply

devices.notes: The ON AIR inscription is not mentioned on the pages read. litt shows ON AIR status by colour, driven from the console's GPO. The mini-USB port is mapped to usb-b. The installation briefing and catalog PDFs were listed on the downloads page but not opened. The brochure PDF was opened and confirms the 5 colours and USB/Lighthouse programming.

conflicts.note: Same page gives two upper limits.

tekpractice.sim_value_reason: Console GPO -> Phoenix GPI per colour: the standard ON-AIR tally wiring lesson.

devices.technology: Two-line digital telephone hybrid (analog phone lines), with send AGC/limiter, receive 'Smart AGC', feedback reduction; AES/EBU version available
devices.why_it_is_a_classic: Telos is the reference brand for broadcast telephone hybrids, and the Hx1/Hx2 are its compact analog-line models. The Hx2 shows the classic hybrid wiring: a mix-minus send in, caller audio out, a telco line and a phone set.

key_specs.line_interface: Universal interface for worldwide application; RJ ports for telco input and phoneset
key_specs.send_input: XLR Female, Pin 2 High (Active Balanced with RF Protection); 2 for Hx2 (one per hybrid)
key_specs.receive_output: XLR Male, Pin 3 High (Active Balanced, RF suppressed)
key_specs.digital_option: AES/EBU version with built-in sample-rate converter
key_specs.processing: Telos Exclusive Feedback Reduction Functions; AGC/Limiter (send); Smart AGC / Platform Leveler (receive)
key_specs.remote_control: DB9 remote control connector with GPIO closures for hybrid control and status indicator lamps
key_specs.power: Internal auto-ranging, 90–265 VAC auto-switching, 50–60 Hz; 100 Watts

connectors.role: send inputs (mix-minus from console), one per hybrid
receive outputs (caller audio), one per hybrid

manuals.title: Telos Hx1 and Hx2 user manual (web)

devices.notes: Specs come from the product page only (no second source opened). The page says 'RJ ports' for telco and phone set but does not name RJ11; the RJ11 telco jacks are mapped to rj45 (closest id; 'rj11' proposed) and the phone-set count of 2 is assumed. 'pots-telephone-line' is a proposed signal id. The send input is where the console's mix-minus (N-1) is patched.

tekpractice.sim_value_reason: Teaches mix-minus send vs caller receive: the classic N-1 / feedback lesson.

devices.technology: Single automatic digital telephone balance unit (TBU) in 1U, adaptive echo cancellation, analog mic/line or AES/EBU I/O on XLR, Ethernet web GUI
devices.why_it_is_a_classic: Sonifex (UK) makes the European-style 'TBU' (telephone balance unit) used in European radio. The DHY-04S's XLR inputs accept analogue or AES/EBU, and its echo canceller and line-balance rejection are quantified on the product page.

key_specs.input: Mic/Line/AES-EBU Input: XLR 3 pin female, with push-button mic/line selection
key_specs.echo_cancellation: Fully adaptive echo cancellation to 127msec – default is 24msec
key_specs.line_balance_rejection: 70dB typical line balance rejection; Rejection Ratio: 80-88dB on complex waveforms
key_specs.remotes: 9-way D-type socket; opto-isolated GPI output (DTMF tone recognition)
key_specs.power: Universal 12W power supply: 90 to 250V AC; 47-63Hz; fused 1A

devices.notes: Single source (product page); the handbook was not opened. The 9-way D-type is mapped to gpio-terminal. RJ11 mapped to rj45 ('rj11' proposed connector), 'pots-telephone-line' and 'ethernet-control' (signals) are proposed ids. The IEC inlet is assumed from 'Filtered/fused' universal supply wording. The DHY-04 is a redesign of the DHY-03.

tekpractice.sim_value_reason: XLR in/out that is either analog or AES3 plus an RJ11 line: good 'same connector, different signal' lesson.

devices.technology: Passive-style rack/desk mix-minus (N-1) generator: subtracts the telephone/codec fader signal from the mixer's program to create the feed back to the TBU or codec
devices.why_it_is_a_classic: A dedicated N-1 box, for desks that have no mix-minus bus. Sonifex says it is used when 'callers join on-air shows through telephone hybrids or codecs', which need mix-minus feeds.
typical_uses: creating N-1 for a telephone hybrid
creating N-1 for an IP codec return
small studios with consoles lacking mix-minus buses

key_specs.inputs: 2 x XLR 3 pin female (balanced) (L & R) from the mixer; 1 x XLR 3 pin female (balanced) (L & R) from the telephone fader
key_specs.output: Analogue Output To TBU: 1 x XLR 3 pin male (balanced) (L & R)
key_specs.output_gain: Adjustable -15dB to +12dB, ref 0dBu gain via a multi-turn pot
key_specs.power: Filtered IEC, switchable 110-120V, or 220-240V, fused, 6W max.

devices.notes: In most broadcast consoles N-1 / mix-minus is a built-in bus function (per-channel 'N-1' outputs). A dedicated box like this is the exception, which is why it is the only mix-minus-system device here. Sonifex lists it as the only product in its 'Telephone Mix Minus Generators' category. The page says '(L & R)' for single XLR entries, so the stereo/mono split per connector is unclear. The handbook was not opened.

tekpractice.sim_value_reason: Makes the N-1 concept physical: program in, caller fader in, mix-minus out to the hybrid.
